title: DELPHI parametric organism / design schema

generative_model.formula: parameters = SUM over parents ( weight_i * parent_i.parameter ) + delta
generative_model.note: Any proposed organism has its roots in another, or is a blend of two or more, plus an explicit novel part (the deltas).

THE_HARD_CAVEAT: MORPHOLOGICAL interpolation, not genetic hybridisation. Averaging two species' body parameters says nothing about whether such an animal could be bred, is viable, or is developmentally reachable; genomes do not average. Flying fish and zebrafish are not crossable. This is a shape, not an organism.

design_file.name: string

parents.organism: id of a reference organism or another design

<parameter>.value | scale | add: set absolutely | multiply the blend | offset the blend
<parameter>.evidence: measured | hypothetical | 'measured value, hypothetical transfer' | none

falls_out: derived quantities that must NOT be set by hand because the deltas already fix them

output_manifest_guarantee.provenance_per_parameter: for EVERY parameter: ancestry (which parents at which weights), the parents' own values and kinds, the blended value, whether a delta moved it, the delta's reason and evidence, and the final kind
output_manifest_guarantee.entirely_delta: a parameter whose delta has evidence 'none' has NO ancestor and NO evidence. It is flagged NO_ANCESTOR_NO_EVIDENCE because that is exactly where a claim needs the most scrutiny.
output_manifest_guarantee.moved_parameters: the list of parameters a delta touched, for lean/eliminate/browser-check.mjs

standard_length_m.drives: real-world standard length; sets the metres-per-model-unit scale

body_mass_kg.drives: wet mass; with flight_muscle_fraction sets the girdle muscle volume

body_depth_over_SL.drives: maximum body depth / SL (full depth, not half)

body_section_exponent.drives: superellipse exponent of the trunk cross-section (2 = ellipse)

head_fraction_SL.drives: fraction of SL over which the snout rounds off

peduncle_depth_frac.drives: caudal peduncle depth / maximum body depth

peduncle_width_frac.drives: caudal peduncle width / maximum body width

pectoral_len_over_SL.drives: longest pectoral fin ray, base to tip, / SL

pectoral_span_over_SL.drives: pectoral tip-to-tip span / SL (both fins, across the body)

pectoral_area_over_SL2.drives: area of BOTH pectoral fins together / SL^2 (Park & Choi 2010 A1 = planform area of the pectoral fin PAIR; their mean chord c = A1/S over the full span S confirms A1 covers both fins)

pectoral_ray_count.drives: lepidotrichia per pectoral fin (one named mesh each)

flight_muscle_fraction.drives: pectoral/girdle muscle mass / body mass; sets the VOLUME of pectoral_muscle_L/R, so it visibly thickens the girdle musculature

mesh_detail.drives: global mesh resolution multiplier (1.0 = the committed flying-fish detail)

derived_never_set_directly.pectoral_aspect_ratio: = span2_over_area_both (kept under this name for existing readers): tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / area of BOTH pectoral fins together. This IS the Park & Choi 2010 convention, AR = S^2/A1 with A1 the planform area of the fin pair (L3: 0.261^2/0.006377 = 10.68). Before 2.0.0 this text wrongly said 'area of ONE fin'; the number was always the both-fins arithmetic.
derived_never_set_directly.span2_over_area_both: tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / area of BOTH pectoral fins together = Park & Choi 2010 AR (S^2/A1)
derived_never_set_directly.aspect_ratio_one_fin: (span/2)^2 / (area of ONE pectoral fin) = span2_over_area_both / 2: one fin treated as a wing from the body midline to its tip. No fetched source uses it; it is here so 'one-fin AR' has one unambiguous meaning. NOTE span^2 / one-fin area (= 2 x Park & Choi) matches no source and is not stored.
derived_never_set_directly.span2_over_wing_area_fish1990: tip-to-tip pectoral span^2 / (both pectoral + both pelvic fin areas): Fish 1990's AR, whose 'wing area' is pectoral + pelvic fins plus the body rectangles between each fin pair (J Zool 221:391, Methods). The body rectangles are not modelled, so this is an UPPER BOUND on the Fish-1990 value. Fish's 3.0-16.9 range is in this convention, not Park & Choi's.
derived_never_set_directly.lifting_area_m2: pectoral (both) + pelvic (both) + caudal membrane area measured on the mesh. NOTE: physics/flier's reference area 0.012688 m2 is Park & Choi's A = A1 + A2 + A3, where A3 = 0.004474 m2 is the BODY planform, not the caudal fin; the mesh's caudal membrane stands in for A3 here (see CHANGELOG 2.0.0, open item)
derived_never_set_directly.flight_muscle_volume_m3: flight_muscle_fraction * body_mass / 1060 kg/m3 (teleost muscle density, assumed)

park_choi_2010.citation: Park H, Choi H 2010 J Exp Biol 213:3269-3279 doi:10.1242/jeb.046052 (physics/prior-art/raw/wb-park-choi-2010.txt)
park_choi_2010.S: wing span of the pectoral fins, tip to tip (Fig. 2; 'S is the full span')
park_choi_2010.A1: planform area of the pectoral fins: the PAIR. Evidence: List of symbols defines the mean chord c = A1/S over the full span; Table 1 L3 gives c = 24 mm = 6377 mm2 / 261 mm (were A1 one fin, its chord over its own half span would be 49 mm and c = A1/S would be half of it); and A1 = 6377 mm2 is smaller than A = A1+A2+A3 = 12688 mm2, which it could not be if the pair were 12754 mm2
park_choi_2010.values: L1 9.0, L2 9.7, L3 10.7 (Table 1, 'based on the pectoral fins only')

fish_1990.citation: Fish FE 1990 J Zool 221:391-403 doi:10.1111/j.1469-7998.1990.tb04009.x (full text: health-sciences.wcupa.edu/sciences-mathematics/biology/fFish/documents/1990JZWing design.pdf)
fish_1990.span: twice the fin base-to-tip distance plus the body width (tip to tip)
fish_1990.wing_area: pectoral + pelvic fins continuous through the body: one side traced and doubled, plus the body rectangles between each fin pair (Methods; Fig. 1a)
fish_1990.values: 3.0-16.9 across 199 ethanol-preserved specimens of 33 species, 6 genera, maximum in Exocoetus; Cypselurus AR = 12.717 M^0.163 (Table III), i.e. about 8.0 at 0.06 kg
fish_1990.repo_name: span2_over_wing_area_fish1990 (upper bound: body rectangles not modelled)
fish_1990.cross_check: Park & Choi L3 in Fish's convention: 0.261^2 / (0.006377 + 0.001837 + body rectangles) <= 8.29, against Fish's Cypselurus regression 8.0 at that mass. The two papers agree once the area is matched; 10.68 vs 3.0-16.9 is NOT a like-for-like comparison

aspect_ratio_conventions.tff_design_ar_9: physics/flier/design.py's AR 9.0 is span^2 / A with A = A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform): a third convention; the real L3 fish is 5.37 on it
